title: how a user prompt gets file pointers injected (prompt-time file injection)
summary: With the embedder opted in, every Claude user prompt that survives the reducer gets up to 3 FILE pointers appended after the notebook notes: the hook reduces the prompt to identifiers + nouns, runs `coldstart find --json` on those terms in a child process, and find itself re-ranks its top 25 against the FULL prompt's embedding before the hook takes the top 3 non-test rows. There is no confidence gate beyond the reducer skip (measured on v-prompt1 dev: nothing cheap separated need/no-need prompts), so non-trivial prompts always get pointers; not opted in, a slash command, or < 2 reduced terms = silent. Built 2026-11-17 as embedder step 4, default-off until the step-5 eval.

invariants: Readers never embed files: a pool file without a stored vector just gets no embedding vote; < 50% of eligible pool vectorised → no re-rank.
Hook-injected text (slash-command expansions) is never reduced or used for injection.
Re-rank weights are the pilot's (fit on arches benchmark prompts), not refit; the shape rule is the pilot's own (>= 40% id-like tokens → no re-rank).

title: how a user prompt gets file pointers injected (prompt-time file injection)
summary: With the embedder opted in, every Claude user prompt that survives the reducer gets up to 3 FILE pointers appended after the notebook notes: the hook reduces the prompt to identifiers + nouns, runs `coldstart find --json` on those terms in a child process, and find itself re-ranks its top 25 against the FULL prompt's embedding before the hook takes the top 3 non-test, non-vendor rows. There is no confidence gate beyond the reducer skip (measured on v-prompt1 dev: nothing cheap separated need/no-need prompts), so non-trivial prompts always get pointers; not opted in, a slash command (`/word`, NOT an absolute path like `/Users/x/a.ts is broken`), or < 2 reduced terms = silent. Built 2026-11-17 as embedder step 4, default-off until the step-5 eval; Opus-reviewed 2026-11-18 (fixes: vendored bundles could be pointers, notes+files payload could exceed the host's 10 KB cap, pasted >80-char tokens became find terms).
